tools.name: publicrecords--calibration-ledger
tools.title: Calibration Ledger — trust a forecast, with evidence (beta)
tools.description:
Calibration Ledger — trust a forecast, with evidence (beta). Given a claim from an organization (IMF, OECD, Fed/FOMC, SPF, ECB SPF, or a listed issuer), returns that organization's track record: error distribution, intervals, bias, band coverage, worst misses with source links — or honest 'no coverage' (free). Organizations only, never people.

When to use: Use when someone cites a forecast from an institution (IMF, OECD, Fed/FOMC, SPF, ECB SPF or a listed issuer) and you need to know how accurate that institution's past forecasts were. Returns error distribution, bias and worst misses with source links, or an explicit no-coverage answer.

Returns: the run's dataset rows as structured JSON (one row per result), plus the run and dataset IDs for paging the full dataset.

Behavior: starts one run of the Apify Actor "publicrecords/calibration-ledger" through Apify's hosted MCP gateway (mcp.apify.com) with your own APIFY_TOKEN; the run uses your Apify account. Read-only: it only reads public web data and changes nothing on the source site. Docs: https://apify.com/publicrecords/calibration-ledger

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: text = hand it a sentence ("The IMF expects Canada's economy to grow 1.8% in 2027"). lookup/score/compare use structured fields.

claim_text.title: Claim (text mode)
claim_text.description: Free-text claim for text mode (e.g. "The IMF expects Canada's economy to grow 1.8% in 2027"). Example: "The IMF expects Canada's economy to grow 1.8% in 2027."

source.title: Source organization
source.description: imf_weo | oecd_eo | fed_sep | spf | ecb_spf | pbo, or an issuer name; optional in text mode Example: "oecd_eo"

series.title: Series
series.description: Generated from rules.yaml — every series the ledger resolves. Example: "RGDP_GROWTH_A"

geo.title: Geography (ISO3 / EA / USA)
geo.description: ISO3 country code, EA, or USA. Required for most score/lookup/compare calls. Example: "CAN"

target_period.title: Target period (YYYY, YYYYQn, YYYY-MM)
target_period.description: Target period as YYYY, YYYYQn, or YYYY-MM when looking up a specific claim. Example: "2027"

point.title: Claimed value
point.description: Numeric claimed value for lookup mode (string so decimals stay exact). Example: "1.8"

published_at.title: Claim date (YYYY-MM-DD)
published_at.description: When the claim was published (YYYY-MM-DD), for lookup/verify. Example: "2026-06-01"

horizon_bucket.title: Horizon bucket
horizon_bucket.description: Optional horizon bucket filter for score mode.

band_kind.title: Band kind (score mode)
band_kind.description: For Fed SEP score mode: central_tendency or range.

claim_id.title: Claim id (verify mode)
claim_id.description: Ledger claim id for verify mode.

issuer.title: Issuer (issuer mode)
issuer.description: Organization name as it appears on its releases/filings (e.g. Salesforce Inc). Both records are returned: dated promises (newswires) and numeric guidance (EDGAR).

Built for algorithmic trading systems, AI trading agents, RAG pipelines, and financial research. Filter by country, importance, category, and date range.

Returns: the run's dataset rows as structured JSON (one row per result), plus the run and dataset IDs for paging the full dataset.

timeZone.title: TimeZone
timeZone.description: Time zone in GMT +/- hours:minutes format (e.g., 'GMT +2:00'). If not provided, the local GMT time zone will be used.

timeFilter.title: Time Filter
timeFilter.description: Determines how time is displayed: 'time_only' shows the event time, 'time_remain' shows remaining time until event. Default is 'time_only'. Options: time_only = Time Only; time_remain = Time Remaining.

importances.title: Importances
importances.description: List of importance ratings for events. Can contain 'high', 'medium', and 'low'. If empty or null, all importance ratings including holidays will be considered. Options: high = High; medium = Medium; low = Low;  = All.

categories.title: Categories
categories.description: List of categories to which the events will be related to. If empty or null, all available categories will be taken into consideration. Example: ""

country.title: Country
country.description: A single country to retrieve economic calendar events for (e.g. United States, Euro Zone). To select several countries, use "Countries (multiple)" below. Leave both blank to include all countries. Example: ""

countries.title: Countries (multiple)
countries.description: Select one or more countries/regions. Combined with "Country" above. Leave empty (and Country blank) to include all countries.

fromDate.title: From Date
fromDate.description: Start date for retrieving the economic calendar in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format. If not provided, only the current day's economic calendar will be retrieved.

toDate.title: To Date
toDate.description: End date for retrieving the economic calendar in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format. If not provided, only the current day's economic calendar will be retrieved.

tools.name: scrapemint--stock-earnings-estimates
tools.title: Stock Earnings Estimates & Results: EPS Forecast vs Actual
tools.description:
Stock Earnings Estimates & Results: EPS Forecast vs Actual. Keyless earnings data for any US stock from NASDAQ: what analysts expect the company to earn next quarter, what it actually earned in past quarters, the percentage it beat or missed by, how often it has beaten, and whether analysts raised or cut their forecast in the last four weeks.

When to use: Use when you need analyst EPS estimates vs reported earnings for a US stock, beat/miss history and recent estimate revisions.

Returns: the run's dataset rows as structured JSON (one row per result), plus the run and dataset IDs for paging the full dataset.

Behavior: starts one run of the Apify Actor "scrapemint/stock-earnings-estimates" through Apify's hosted MCP gateway (mcp.apify.com) with your own APIFY_TOKEN; the run uses your Apify account. Read-only: it only reads public web data and changes nothing on the source site. Docs: https://apify.com/scrapemint/stock-earnings-estimates

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: summary = one row per ticker: what analysts expect next quarter, what the company delivered last quarter, how often it has beaten, and whether estimates are being raised or cut. surprises = one row per reported quarter. forecasts = one row per forecast period. Options: summary = Summary (one row per ticker); surprises = Surprises (reported quarters); forecasts = Forecasts (forward estimates).

symbols.title: Symbols
symbols.description: US tickers to look up, e.g. NVDA, TSLA, AAPL. Maximum 200 per run.

minBeatRate.title: Min beat rate (%)
minBeatRate.description: Keep only companies that beat expectations in at least this share of their reported quarters. 75 returns serial beaters. 0 = no filter.

onlyRaisedEstimates.title: Only where estimates are rising
onlyRaisedEstimates.description: Keep only tickers where more analysts raised their forecast than cut it in the last four weeks. Estimate revision direction is the forward looking half of this data.

includeAnnual.title: Include annual forecasts (forecasts mode)
includeAnnual.description: Return full year estimates alongside the quarterly ones.

maxRows.title: Max rows per run
maxRows.description: Cap on rows returned across all tickers. Controls total cost.

timeRange.title: Time Range

tools.name: ryanclinton--wayback-machine-search
tools.title: Wayback Machine Scraper - Track Website Changes Over Time
tools.description:
Wayback Machine Scraper - Track Website Changes Over Time. Search the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine for historical snapshots of any website. Retrieve archived page metadata -- including timestamps, URLs, MIME types, HTTP status codes, and content hashes -- for up to 10,000 snapshots per run.

When to use: Use when you need archived Wayback Machine snapshots of a URL or domain over time, e.g. to see what a page said on a past date.

Returns: the run's dataset rows as structured JSON (one row per result), plus the run and dataset IDs for paging the full dataset.

Behavior: starts one run of the Apify Actor "ryanclinton/wayback-machine-search" through Apify's hosted MCP gateway (mcp.apify.com) with your own APIFY_TOKEN; the run uses your Apify account. Read-only: it only reads public web data and changes nothing on the source site. Docs: https://apify.com/ryanclinton/wayback-machine-search

monitor.title: Monitor mode (one-flag scheduled monitoring)
monitor.description: Turn on for scheduled monitoring runs. One flag enables: change detection, only-changed snapshots, change intelligence + diffs, alerts on moderate-or-major changes, timeline output, insights record, AND delta-since-last-run state tracking. Compose with a Use Case preset for industry-specific defaults.

deltaSinceLastRun.title: Delta since last run (return only what's new)
deltaSinceLastRun.description: Turn on for stateful monitoring without external storage. The actor remembers the events and snapshot URLs returned in the previous run (in a named key-value store) and filters this run to only the events / snapshots that are NEW since then. First run for a given URL set returns everything as new.

monitorStateKey.title: Monitor state key (advanced)
monitorStateKey.description: Optional override for the key-value-store key used by Delta mode. Auto-derived from the sorted URL list if not set; provide a stable string here if you want to share state across separate runs that have different URL inputs (e.g. weekly batch + ad-hoc spot-checks).

useCase.title: Use Case (one-click preset)
useCase.description: Pick a preset to auto-configure filters, change detection, and output mode for a common workflow. Set to "custom" to use the raw inputs below. SEO = monthly buckets + 200-only + change-only. Compliance = closest-date evidence with content. Competitor = monthly buckets + only-changed + alerts on moderate-or-major. Forensics = full-domain crawl, no collapsing. Options: custom = Custom (use the inputs below as-is); seo = SEO history audit; compliance = Legal / compliance evidence; competitor = Com…

url.title: URL
url.description: URL or domain to search for snapshots (e.g., "example.com" or "https://example.com/page"). Ignored if you supply a list under URLs (batch). Console UI prefills "apify.com" as a placeholder; programmatic API runs only use this field if you explicitly send it. Example: "apify.com"

urls.title: URLs (batch / comparative)
urls.description: Optional: query multiple URLs in one run for comparative competitive intelligence. Each URL gets its own snapshots, change detection, and metrics in the output. The single URL above is added if both fields are populated.

matchType.title: Match Type
matchType.description: How to match the URL. "exact" = exact URL only, "prefix" = URL prefix match, "host" = all pages on same host, "domain" = all subdomains too Options: exact = Exact URL; prefix = URL Prefix; host = Same Host; domain = All Subdomains.

dateFrom.title: Date From
dateFrom.description: Start date filter (YYYYMMDD or YYYY format, e.g., "20200101" or "2020")

dateTo.title: Date To
dateTo.description: End date filter (YYYYMMDD or YYYY format, e.g., "20231231" or "2023")

targetDate.title: Target Date (closest-snapshot lookup)
targetDate.description: Return the single snapshot closest to this date — useful for legal/compliance evidence ("what did the page say on 2020-06-15?"). Accepts YYYY-MM-DD or YYYYMMDD. When set, overrides Max Results and returns one snapshot with distanceFromTargetDays.

statusFilter.title: Status Code Filter
statusFilter.description: HTTP status code filter (e.g., "200" for successful pages only)

mimeFilter.title: MIME Type Filter
mimeFilter.description: MIME type filter (e.g., "text/html" for HTML pages only)

collapseBy.title: Collapse Duplicates
collapseBy.description: Collapse duplicate snapshots. "digest" = unique content only, "timestamp:6" = one per month, "timestamp:8" = one per day, "timestamp:10" = one per hour Options:  = No collapsing; digest = Unique content only (digest); timestamp:6 = One per month; timestamp:8 = One per day; timestamp:10 = One per hour.

fastLatest.title: Fast Latest (recency optimization)
fastLatest.description: Return the most recent snapshots faster by skipping older index segments. Only useful for domains with hundreds of thousands of snapshots — combine with Max Results to fetch the latest N quickly.

autoPaginate.title: Auto-paginate beyond 10,000 results
autoPaginate.description: When the CDX API hits its 10,000-row cap, automatically chunk the query year-by-year and merge the results — letting you pull full multi-year domain histories in one run. Costs more proxy time; only enable when you need the complete archive.

maxResults.title: Max Results (per URL)
maxResults.description: Maximum number of snapshots to return per URL (max 10,000 in a single CDX query — enable Auto-paginate to exceed). Ignored when Target Date is set (always returns one snapshot).

detectChanges.title: Detect Changes Between Snapshots
detectChanges.description: Compare each snapshot to the previous one and flag rows where the content hash or HTTP status changed. Adds a "changed" boolean and "changeType" string to every result. Free — uses metadata you already have.

onlyChanged.title: Only Return Changed Snapshots
onlyChanged.description: Filter results to only the snapshots where the page actually changed (plus the first "initial" baseline). Requires Detect Changes. Turns 1,000 raw snapshots into ~50 actionable rows.

changeIntelligence.title: Change Intelligence (magnitude + categories + key diffs)
changeIntelligence.description: Augment every changed row with a changeSummary (magnitude: minor/moderate/major, categories: pricing/legal/product/layout/etc., keyDiffs: human-readable change phrases) and a structured diff (added/removed text, change score). Best results require Include Page Content so the actor can diff actual text.

alertOnMagnitude.title: Alert when changes hit this severity
alertOnMagnitude.description: Emit a single "alert" record at the top of the dataset when changes meet the threshold. Pairs well with scheduling: connect a webhook → Slack/email when the alert record fires. Requires Change Intelligence to compute magnitude. Options: none = No alert (default); any = Any change; moderate = Moderate or major change; major = Major change only.

query.title: Historical diff search (keyword)
query.description: Filter the output to only snapshots whose change content matches a keyword. Searches changeSummary categories (e.g. "pricing"), keyDiffs, added/removed text, and full content. Pure post-filter — no extra API calls. Example: query "pricing" returns only the snapshots where pricing changed.

includeInsights.title: Emit Insights record (default ON)
includeInsights.description: Push a single "insights" record at the top of the dataset with key events, risk signals, business signals, typed events, coverage, cross-URL comparison, and chartData. Turn off if you only want raw rows.

outputMode.title: Output Mode
outputMode.description: What records to emit. "Snapshots" = one row per snapshot (default). "Timeline" = one row per stable version (consecutive identical-digest snapshots collapsed). "Report" = a markdown report in the key-value store + version records + a summary record. Options: snapshots = Snapshots (one row per archive); timeline = Timeline (one row per distinct version); report = Report (markdown + versions).

generateReport.title: Generate Markdown Report
generateReport.description: Always write a REPORT.md to the run's key-value store, even when Output Mode is "snapshots". Useful when you want both raw rows and a human-readable summary.

includeContent.title: Include Page Content
includeContent.description: Fetch and include the archived page text content. Required for the diff/keyDiffs fields under Change Intelligence. Slow — fetches each snapshot individually with polite rate limiting.

maxContentFetch.title: Max Pages to Fetch Content
maxContentFetch.description: Maximum number of pages to fetch content for (only used if Include Page Content is enabled)

useJsRender.title: Use JavaScript Rendering
useJsRender.description: Enable Playwright rendering for archived pages that return as empty React/Next/Gatsby SPA shells (notably HubSpot, late-2024+ Atlassian). Off (default) uses a cheap HTTP fetch only — fastest and cheapest, but returns empty shells for modern SPA pricing pages. Pair with `forceJsRender` to control whether every snapshot is rendered or only the ones that look like SPA shells.

forceJsRender.title: Always Render (no cheap-fetch first)
forceJsRender.description: If `useJsRender` is on, render every snapshot via Playwright instead of falling back from a cheap HTTP fetch. Use when you already know your URLs are SPA shells and don't want to pay for the cheap-fetch attempt. Ignored when `useJsRender` is off.

proxyConfiguration.title: Proxy Configuration
proxyConfiguration.description: Proxy used to reach the Wayback Machine CDX API and archived pages. Defaults to AUTO — Apify's smart router uses datacenter IPs where they work and falls back to residential where blocked. Switch to RESIDENTIAL explicitly if you see persistent 403s. Example: {"useApifyProxy":true}

useApifyProxy.description: Use Apify Proxy for requests. Leave the default unless the Actor's README says otherwise.

tools.name: data_xplorer--google-news-scraper-fast
tools.title: Google News Scraper
tools.description:
Google News Scraper. Scrape Google News in real time, including images and descriptions. This tool extracts complete structured data: high-resolution visuals, full, titles, sources, dates, and direct URLs.

When to use: Use when you need recent Google News articles for a query (title, source, date, URL, image).

Returns: the run's dataset rows as structured JSON (one row per result), plus the run and dataset IDs for paging the full dataset.

Behavior: starts one run of the Apify Actor "data_xplorer/google-news-scraper-fast" through Apify's hosted MCP gateway (mcp.apify.com) with your own APIFY_TOKEN; the run uses your Apify account. Read-only: it only reads public web data and changes nothing on the source site. Docs: https://apify.com/data_xplorer/google-news-scraper-fast

keywords.title: Search Keywords
keywords.description: List of keywords to search for. You can use Google News search operators: - Use '-' to exclude words (e.g. 'bitcoin -ethereum') - Use 'site:' to filter by specific website (e.g. 'bitcoin site:cnn.com') - Use 'OR' to search for multiple terms (e.g. 'bitcoin OR ethereum') - Use quotes for exact match (e.g. '"bitcoin price"')

topics.title: News Topics
topics.description: Select one or more predefined Google News topics to scrape.

topicUrls.title: Custom Topic / Section URLs
topicUrls.description: Provide custom Google News topic or section URLs to scrape. Useful for niche topics not in the predefined list. Example: https://news.google.com/topics/CAAqJggKIiBDQkFTRWdvSUwyMHZNRGx1YlY4U0FtVnVHZ0pWVXlnQVAB

maxArticles.title: Maximum News
maxArticles.description: Maximum number of news to extract per keyword or topic (0 = no limit)

timeframe.title: Time Period (Only for keywords)
timeframe.description: Time period for the news search. Note: this filter applies mainly to keyword searches. Topic pages return their own curated results. Options: 1h = Last hour; 1d = Last day; 7d = Last week; 30d = Last month; 1y = Last year; all = Anytime.

region_language.title: Region and Language
region_language.description: Region and language for news search

decodeUrls.title: Decode Google News URLs
decodeUrls.description: If enabled, decodes Google News URLs to get the original article URLs. Note: This will significantly slow down the scraping process as each URL needs to be decoded individually.

extractDescriptions.title: Extract Article Descriptions
extractDescriptions.description: If enabled, extracts the meta description from each article page. Note: This will significantly slow down the scraping process.

extractImages.title: Extract Article Images
extractImages.description: Fetches the og:image from each article page when no image is available (mainly for RSS/topic results). When this option is not explicitly set, images are extracted by default. Toggle OFF to skip image extraction and speed up scraping.

proxyConfiguration.title: Proxy Configuration
proxyConfiguration.description: Configure Apify Proxy. Residential proxies recommended for best results.

useApifyProxy.description: Use Apify Proxy for requests. Leave the default unless the Actor's README says otherwise.
